description: Public-safe status manifest for MMIR.ai. Internal QA, agent instructions and deploy reports stay in the private control repo; this browser payload contains only product-safe status copy.

components.label: MMIR public site
components.notes: The static app shell is served from the public Pages artifact.

components.label: Latest deploy verification
components.notes: The public artifact is checked by GitHub Actions before deploy. Current public copy includes the stale repair resume expiry guard, active route policy strip and refreshed trust manifest so demo viewers can see local, hosted and fallback route boundaries.

components.label: Public URL health
components.notes: External checks have seen MMIR content, but some networks may still block or rate-limit a newly registered custom domain. Treat this as a network/domain-reputation watch until checked from another network.

components.label: Domain availability watch
components.notes: Latest Pages deploy is green for the verified baseline and DNS resolves through Cloudflare. Keep this watch generic and public-safe when diagnosing network/domain-reputation failures.

components.label: No-model deploy proof
components.notes: The public chat shell includes a no-model fallback path, free route floor, stale repair resume expiry, refreshed trust manifest and visible active-route policy without exposing internal QA reports.

components.label: GitHub Pages origin
components.notes: The default GitHub Pages URL redirects to the custom domain while public/CNAME is present. The status panel also checks the latest public Pages deploy run.

components.label: Domain reputation
components.notes: Some corporate networks may temporarily block newly registered domains. Test from mobile data or ask for allowlisting if this happens.

components.label: Managed API
components.notes: Managed provider routing requires auth, rate limits, audit logging and server-side provider secrets before public launch.

components.label: Local node
components.notes: Local health is checked only when the user activates a local backend profile in this browser; node handoff remains user-controlled and localhost-first.
